questions.q: In the Meridian Outfitters environment, what makes meridian-public-subnet "public"?
options: Being the first subnet created in the VPC
A route to an internet gateway plus map-public-ip-on-launch enabled — not one setting alone
Having a larger CIDR block than the private subnet
The word "public" in its tag name
questions.explain: A subnet only behaves as public once it has a route to an internet gateway AND assigns public IPs to new instances — both pieces, not either one.

questions.q: Why does meridian-app1 get no public IP address at launch?
options: It was launched without a security group
It launches into the private subnet, which was never given map-public-ip-on-launch or a route to the internet gateway
Public IPs must be requested from AWS support separately
AWS never assigns public IPs to t3.micro instances
questions.explain: meridian-app1's subnet has no internet gateway route and no public-IP-on-launch setting, so it stays privately addressed by design.

questions.q: Why does Meridian's shared app data go into an S3 bucket instead of a local EBS volume on one of the instances?
options: S3 buckets are free while EBS volumes are not
Both the web and app tier instances need to read and write the same data, and local disk on one instance isn't reachable from the other
EBS volumes cannot be attached to t3.micro instances
S3 is required for any data touched by more than one AWS service
questions.explain: Shared data that multiple tiers need isn't a good fit for one instance's local disk — S3 gives both tiers the same access point.

questions.q: Why must the S3 bucket be named meridian-outfitters-app-data rather than just app-data?
options: S3 bucket names are unique across all of AWS, not just within one account
It has no effect — either name would have worked identically
Bucket names must always start with the company name by AWS policy
Short bucket names are reserved for AWS's own internal use
questions.explain: S3's bucket namespace is global, so a generic name like "app-data" is almost certainly already taken by someone else's account.

questions.q: At the end of this lesson, what is true about meridian-web-sg and meridian-app-sg?
options: Both already allow SSH from anywhere on the internet
They were merged into a single security group shared by both tiers
Both were created with zero inbound rules — scoping access is Lesson 30's job
Only meridian-web-sg exists; meridian-app-sg is created in Lesson 30
questions.explain: This lesson only stands the environment up; both security groups start locked down and get scoped to their real traffic in Lesson 30.
